title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When you pay a growth multiple for capitalized costs, you are paying twice—once for the asset and once when it amortizes.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.html: Checking the 13 November 2026 market tape reveals the core valuation gap in SoftTech Engineers Ltd (NSE: SOFTTECH). At ₹425.90, market cap stands at ₹588.29 Cr (Screener: ₹590 Cr) [1, 23]. The stock trades at 118.89x TTM earnings and 3.40x book value (₹125 per share) [1, 23]. That is not a distressed micro-cap price. It is a rich SaaS multiple paid for a firm with a 2.77% ROE, a 6.31% ROCE, and eight straight years of negative free cash flow [1, 2].

Why does SoftTech trade at 119x earnings instead of 15x? Buyers look past thin statutory net profit (₹5.33 Cr in FY26; ₹3.58 Cr TTM implied by 118.89x P/E) [1, 2]. Instead, they focus on two top-line stories. First, FY26 sales rose +39.5% YoY to ₹132.90 Cr (TTM ₹144 Cr) [1, 2]. Second, the H1 FY27 order book reached ₹302.35 Cr, led by the ₹92.95 Cr JNPA AI Digital Twin deal [3]. On EV/Sales (~4.2x TTM sales of ₹144 Cr), bulls view SoftTech as a cheap GovTech-to-SaaS play. They argue upfront engineering spend is only masking future operating leverage.

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹425.90, buyers are already paying for a full SaaS transformation, 22%+ revenue growth AND a 15%+ FCF margin, that has not yet appeared in audited cash flows.

web_blocks.html: A Reverse Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) test shows how little margin of safety exists at ₹425.90. We use a 12.5% cost of equity for a ₹588 Cr illiquid small-cap with 18.89% promoter holding [1]. At an enterprise value near ₹600 Cr, the price bakes in 22%–25% annual revenue growth for ten years. It also requires free cash flow margins to jump from -1.0% today to 14%–16% [1, 2]. Here is the catch. Suppose SoftTech grows 25% a year while still capitalizing ₹30+ Cr/year of software and holding ₹53.52 Cr of unbilled assets [2]. Intrinsic equity value stays far below ₹425.90 because cash never reaches owners [2].

web_blocks.caption: Peer Valuation & Capital Efficiency Matrix (As of 13 Nov 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: SOFTTECH trades at 6.1x NEWGEN's P/E multiple and 3.8x MAPMYINDIA's P/E while delivering less than a quarter of their ROE and ROCE.

web_blocks.html: The peer comparison is devastating for the current valuation. Newgen Software (NEWGEN) has a ₹6,256.90 Cr market cap and trades at 19.6x TTM P/E with an 18.5% TTM ROE (25.0% Screener ROCE) [25]. C.E. Info Systems (MAPMYINDIA) trades at 31.7x TTM P/E with a 17.1% TTM ROE (19.1% Screener ROCE) [26]. Ramco Systems (RAMCOSYS) trades at 71.3x TTM P/E with an 8.7% TTM ROE [27]. Geospatial peer Genesys International (GENESYS) trades at 37.8x TTM P/E with a 5.7% TTM ROE [28]. Paying 118.89x P/E for SoftTech's 2.77% ROE fails every relative-value test.

web_blocks.title: Valuation Anchor: What Is SoftTech Actually Worth Today?
paragraphs: Start with normalized owner earnings. Take FY26 EBITDA (₹33.0 Cr) and deduct cash capex/capitalized R&D (₹32.57 Cr) plus ₹12.08 Cr of credit-loss provisions [2]. True economic free cash flow is near zero or negative [2].

Suppose mid-cycle FCF reaches ₹15–18 Cr (a 10% FCF margin on ₹150–180 Cr sales). A 20x multiple yields ₹300–360 Cr, or roughly ₹220–₹260 per share. Even a generous 2.5x Price-to-Sales multiple on ₹144 Cr TTM sales implies ~₹260–₹320 per share. At ₹425.90, the stock is priced for perfection.

web_blocks.html: Historical multiple bands reinforce why ₹425.90 is fragile. Over the past five years, SoftTech's capitalized software wave repeatedly compressed statutory PAT. The market intermittently bid the stock to 90x–130x trailing P/E on order-book announcements. Yet the stock suffered 30%–50% drawdowns whenever amortization rose or municipal collections stalled [1, 2]. By contrast, Newgen Software (19.6x TTM P/E, 18.5% ROE) and MapmyIndia (31.7x TTM P/E, 17.1% ROE) trade at far lower multiples while converting EBITDA into free cash flow [25, 26].

A forward sensitivity check confirms the valuation hurdle. Suppose FY27 revenue rises +25% to ₹166 Cr at a 25% EBITDA margin (₹41.5 Cr). Annualizing Q2 FY27 depreciation (₹6.85 Cr) implies ~₹27.4 Cr of D&A [1]. Subtracting ₹3.8 Cr of interest and a 35% tax rate leaves ~₹6.7 Cr PAT (~₹4.85/share on 1.38 Cr shares) [1, 2]. Even after a +25% revenue year, ₹425.90 equals ~88x forward earnings with near-zero free cash flow.

Valuation Change Trigger: Upgrade from valuation rejection only after two straight quarters of positive free cash flow and a forward EV/FCF below 22x. That requires FCF above ₹27 Cr/year or a share price below ₹260–₹300.

book_paragraphs: Once we lift the blindfold and look at the market screen as of 13 November 2026, you can see why separating our business audit from the stock price matters so much. If you had started with the price, ₹425.90, up nearly 20% over the past year and sitting on a ₹588 Cr market cap, you might have assumed the market knew something extraordinary about the next three years of earnings.

Instead, when you lay the ₹425.90 price tag next to the audited cash-flow statement we just dissected in Chapter 6, the math becomes sobering. At ₹425.90, SoftTech trades at 118.89 times trailing earnings and 3.40 times book value. Those are elite compounder multiples, yet the underlying capital engine is earning a 2.77% return on equity and has not produced a single rupee of positive cumulative free cash flow in eight years.

Let us run a Reverse DCF together across the desk. Don't ask what target price we can invent; ask what the market is already assuming at ₹425.90. At a 12.5% discount rate, fair for an illiquid micro-cap, you need SoftTech to grow revenue at 22% to 25% every year for a decade AND convert 15% of every revenue rupee into free cash flow by Year 5. That means the ₹30.50 Cr annual software-capitalization treadmill has to slow down dramatically while the ₹92.95 Cr JNPA project and municipal contracts collect cash on time.

Now look across the street at the Indian listed peer group. Newgen Software, a far larger, cash-rich workflow automation franchise, sells for 19.6 times TTM earnings with an 18.5% ROE and 25.0% ROCE. MapmyIndia. This owns India's premier geospatial digital-twin stack, sells for 31.7 times TTM earnings with a 17.1% ROE. Why would a rational allocator pay 119 times earnings for SoftTech when institutional-grade software compounders are available at a quarter to a sixth of that multiple?

When we compare SoftTech's 118.89x TTM P/E against the Indian software peer set in our snapshot table, the valuation gap is impossible to ignore. Newgen Software delivers a 18.5% ROE and 25.0% ROCE at 19.6x TTM P/E. MapmyIndia delivers a 17.1% ROE and 19.1% ROCE at 31.7x TTM P/E. Ramco Systems delivers an 8.7% ROE at 71.3x TTM P/E. SoftTech delivers a 2.77% ROE and 6.31% ROCE, yet asks you to pay 118.89x earnings.

Let us check the forward earnings math on a conservative napkin. Even if SoftTech grows FY27 revenue another 25% to ₹166 Cr and holds a 25% EBITDA margin (₹41.5 Cr), an annualized ₹27.4 Cr depreciation charge plus ₹3.8 Cr of interest leaves roughly ₹10.3 Cr of pre-tax profit. At a 35% effective tax rate, elevated because foreign subsidiary losses cannot offset Indian standalone taxes, net profit comes to ~₹6.7 Cr, or roughly ₹4.85 per share. At ₹425.90, you are still paying nearly 88x forward earnings for a business that may not generate positive free cash flow.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Price-to-Sales Illusion
book_callouts.text: Small-cap software bulls often retreat to Price-to-Sales (4.1x TTM sales) when P/E looks absurd. Never fall for EV/Sales without checking the R&D capitalization policy. When a company capitalizes 23% of its revenue onto the balance sheet every year instead of expensing it, reported EBITDA looks artificially plump—until the amortization wave catches up.

book_subsections.title: Why Multiple Compression Is the Base Case
paragraphs: There are only two ways a 119x P/E resolves: either earnings explode 4x to 5x while the stock price marks time, or the multiple compresses toward peer levels of 25x–35x. With Q2 FY27 quarterly depreciation already running at ₹6.85 Cr, annualizing to ₹27.4 Cr. And Q2 net profit collapsing to ₹0.21 Cr, earnings explosion faces a steep amortization headwind.

Even if SoftTech executes its ₹302.35 Cr order book cleanly over the next 18 months and lifts EBITDA margins, a realistic base-case valuation of 2.2x to 2.5x forward sales puts fair value closer to ₹300–₹320 per share. Buying at ₹425.90 leaves zero cushion for municipal payment delays or another subsidiary loss.
